Raymond III took full control of Tripoli around 1160. He pursued a policy of independence from the Kingdom of Jerusalem while maintaining ties with Byzantium. In 1164 he allied with Nur ad Din Zangi against the Crusaders but later shifted to support the Frankish cause. He married Eschiva of Bures in 1165 strengthening his links with the nobility of Jerusalem. During the minority of Baldwin IV Raymond served as regent of the kingdom from 1174 to 1176. However tensions grew when Guy of Lusignan became king and Raymond opposed his rule. In 1187 Raymond led a contingent of troops to the Battle of Hattin where he escaped the massacre but returned to Tripoli wounded. After the defeat he worked to organize the defense of his county despite the loss of many Crusader forces.
